record.paper_title: Open Questions in CMR Manganites, Relevance of Clustered States, and Analogies with other Compounds
record.original_question: For explaining colossal magnetoresistance, is there a fundamental physical distinction between theories where the competing phases originate mainly from Jahn-Teller electron-phonon interactions and theories where they originate mainly from Coulomb interactions, and can realistic many-body models produce a large magnetoresistance effect without relying only on phenomenological descriptions?

evidence.quote: For the explanation of CMR, is there a fundamental difference between JT- and Coulomb-based theories? ... Can a large MR effect be obtained with more realistic models?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider strongly correlated electron systems modeling doped manganites of the form R_{1-x}A_x MnO_3 (with R a rare earth and A an alkaline earth), in which the competition between a ferromagnetic metallic phase and an insulating (charge/orbital/antiferromagnetically ordered) phase is believed to underlie the colossal magnetoresistance (CMR) phenomenon — namely a dramatic decrease of electrical resistivity upon application of an external magnetic field near the Curie temperature.

Two broad classes of microscopic many-body Hamiltonians are commonly proposed to generate such competing phases:

(A) Jahn-Teller (JT) electron-phonon models. The Hamiltonian has the schematic form
   H_JT = -Σ_{ij,αβ,σ} t^{αβ}_{ij} c^†_{iασ} c_{jβσ} - J_H Σ_i s_i·S_i + λ Σ_{i,αβ} Q_i^{αβ} c^†_{iα} c_{iβ} + (1/2) Σ_i (P_i^2 + K Q_i^2) + J_{AF} Σ_{⟨ij⟩} S_i·S_j,
 where α,β ∈ {d_{x^2-y^2}, d_{3z^2-r^2}} are e_g orbitals on a Mn lattice, S_i are localized t_{2g} core spins, J_H is the Hund coupling, and Q_i are JT phonon modes coupling to the orbital pseudospin with coupling λ.

(B) Coulomb-interaction-based models. The Hamiltonian has the schematic form
   H_C = -Σ_{ij,αβ,σ} t^{αβ}_{ij} c^†_{iασ} c_{jβσ} - J_H Σ_i s_i·S_i + U Σ_{iα} n_{iα↑} n_{iα↓} + U' Σ_{i,α<β} n_{iα} n_{iβ} + J Σ_{i,α<β} S_{iα}·S_{iβ} + V Σ_{⟨ij⟩} n_i n_j + J_{AF} Σ_{⟨ij⟩} S_i·S_j,
 with on-site and inter-orbital Coulomb repulsions U, U', Hund exchange J, and nearest-neighbour repulsion V, but with no explicit electron-phonon coupling.

Questions:
(1) In the regime of parameters relevant to manganites and near a first-order transition between a ferromagnetic metallic and an insulating phase, is there a fundamental, qualitative, experimentally distinguishable distinction between the low-energy physics produced by Hamiltonians of type (A) and those of type (B)? Equivalently, do these two families belong to the same universality class of phase competition at the relevant scales, or do they yield essentially different predictions for the structure of the inhomogeneous (clustered) states and for transport in a magnetic field?

(2) Can a sharp, large colossal magnetoresistance — i.e. an order-of-magnitude or greater drop in resistivity in response to a magnetic field of order a few Tesla near the magnetic ordering temperature — be derived directly from one of these realistic many-body Hamiltonians (A) or (B), without recourse to purely phenomenological random-resistor / percolation / coexistence postulates, but instead as an emergent consequence of the model's intrinsic dynamics?
artifact.status_search_result: The two questions remain open in the condensed matter community. Reviews and subsequent literature on CMR manganites continue to debate whether JT phonon-based and Coulomb-based scenarios are fundamentally distinct or operationally equivalent, and obtaining a large CMR effect directly from realistic microscopic many-body Hamiltonians (rather than from phenomenological percolative/coexistence models) is still considered an unresolved challenge.

status_evidence.title: Colossal magnetoresistant materials: the key role of phase separation (review)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses competing JT and Coulombic mechanisms for phase separation in manganites and notes that obtaining CMR from realistic microscopic models remains a major theoretical challenge.
status_evidence.claim: The fundamental distinction between JT- and Coulomb-driven phase competition, and microscopic derivation of CMR, is identified as an open problem.
